lines: In 1969, engineers switched off Niagara Falls.
In 1969, engineers SWITCHED OFF Niagara Falls.
Wait, what? You can switch off a waterfall?
Wait, WHAT? You can SWITCH OFF a waterfall?
Well, the American side. And what they found underneath explains why the whole falls is moving.
Well, the AMERICAN side. And what they found UNDERNEATH explains why the whole falls is MOVING.
Okay, so they built a dam of rock across their side of the river. About 28,000 tons of it.
Okay, so they built a DAM of ROCK across their side of the river. About 28,000 TONS of it.
And the falls just went dry?
And the falls just went DRY?
For five months. And at the bottom, they found a huge pile of fallen rock.
For FIVE MONTHS. And at the bottom, they found a HUGE pile of fallen ROCK.
Ooh, where did all that rock come from?
Ooh, where did all that ROCK come from?
The cliff itself. The top layer is hard rock, but underneath, it's soft shale. Basically, packed mud.
The CLIFF itself. The top layer is HARD rock, but underneath, it's SOFT shale. Basically, packed MUD.
Water eats the soft layer away, the hard edge hangs out, and then it snaps off.
Water EATS the soft layer away, the hard edge HANGS out, and then it SNAPS off.
Again and again. 12,000 years ago, it started seven miles downstream.
Again and AGAIN. 12,000 years ago, it started SEVEN MILES downstream.
Seven miles? It's been walking backwards this whole time?
SEVEN MILES? It's been walking BACKWARDS this whole time?
Yep. But today, it's barely moving.
Yep. But today, it's BARELY moving.
Because we take its water. By day, about half the river goes through tunnels to power stations.
Because we TAKE its water. By DAY, about HALF the river goes through TUNNELS to POWER stations.
Even more. So in a way, they still switch off Niagara Falls. A little, every single night.
Even MORE. So in a way, they still SWITCH OFF Niagara Falls. A little, every single NIGHT.
That's amazing! Follow for a new wonder every day!
That's AMAZING! FOLLOW for a new wonder every day!
